summary.intent: Run the full autonomous post-execute-phase ship loop for CipherBox GSD phase 73 (verify, secure, crypto/privacy review, security review, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit CLI review, ship, resolve PR reviews) without babysitting.
summary.outcome: Verification/security/validation gates passed (7/7 verified, 17/17 threats closed, Nyquist compliant); diagnosed and fixed a local TEE-worker port/auth misconfiguration blocking 3 SDK E2E tests, updated a stale test assertion for phase 73's new tombstone-return contract, and fixed a real CodeRabbit-flagged bug in useSharedNavigationActions.ts where refresh-access reseeded stale cached state instead of re-resolving IPNS; SDK E2E reached 106/106 green and the web app typechecked, with commit/ship/PR-review steps still in progress when the transcript ends.

repo: Local dev stack: tee-worker's container port 3001 gets remapped to host :3002 because mock-ipns-routing already claims host :3001, but TeeService defaults TEE_WORKER_URL to http://localhost:3001 — causing silent 404s and an unseeded tee_key_state table at API boot.

The tee-worker's /public-key endpoint is gated by `Authorization: Bearer $TEE_WORKER_SECRET` (apps/tee-worker/src/middleware/auth.ts); the host-run API must be started with a matching TEE_WORKER_SECRET or the pubkey fetch 401s and tee_key_state stays empty.

tee_key_state is populated by the API (TeeKeyStateService) fetching the worker's pubkey at startup, not by the worker itself — so an empty table means the API's boot-time fetch failed, not that the worker container is down.

Phase 73 commit subjects were already conventional (fix(73-08):, test(73-01):) — the filter-branch reword step in the ship-phase runbook was unnecessary; only unrelated chore:/docs: merge-summary descriptions had parens, and those don't drive release-please versioning.
CodeRabbit CLI review flagged two hallucinated cross-references to nonexistent phases (45-55/79-88) in .planning/ doc metadata — treated as noise/discard.

code.finding: publishedParent resolve uses raw resolvePublishedNode, bypassing the ROT-07 signature-verification gate applied to sibling reads elsewhere in the same PR — flagged as non-blocking LOW by both the crypto/privacy and security audits.

refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey reseeded publishedNode from the cached getSharedFolderState() (the same stale node that just failed) instead of re-resolving via IPNS, so a co-writer whose write failed on stale state could never recover via 'Refresh access'. Fixed by mirroring the existing restoreToBreadcrumbIndex pattern: seed then call getSdkClient().refreshSharedFolder(currentShareId) to re-resolve, wrapped in try/catch-ignored.

Test 20 (WRITE-04, tombstone → publish returns 410) asserted the pre-phase-73 throw-on-410 contract via expect(publishError).toBeDefined(); phase 73's createAndPublishIpnsRecord now catches the 410 and returns {success:false, tombstoned:true} instead of throwing. Confirmed no production caller relied on the old throw (the only 410-tombstone consumer, publishNodeFn at client.ts:5177, already handles the tombstoned return correctly), so the test assertion was updated rather than the code.

workflow: When a background command's summary reports exit code 0 but a piped/tee'd command masks the real status, re-check the actual exit code directly rather than trusting the notification summary — one SDK E2E run here was actually exit 1 despite the notification saying completed/0.

Before treating an E2E failure as infra noise, trace it to a specific test and confirm it isn't touching the phase's own changed code path — one of three 'TEE infra' failures turned out to be a real stale-test-contract issue on the phase's SC4 path.

Diagnosing an infra failure methodically (probe both candidate ports directly, compare responses) found a root cause (port collision + auth secret mismatch) that a superficial 'container is running, must be infra noise' judgment would have missed.

friction: SDK E2E gate initially showed 3 failures that looked like generic TEE infra noise, requiring deep diagnosis (container status, DB state, port mapping, auth headers) to separate a genuine local-stack misconfiguration from a real phase regression.
Background task notification reported the SDK E2E run as completed/exit 0 when the actual exit code was 1, requiring a manual re-check of the tail output.

The ship-phase runbook's step 7 (conventional-commit reword via git filter-branch) turned out to be unnecessary for this phase since commits were already conventional, but required verification effort to confirm before skipping.
